answer: A thousand fake names cost a farm almost nothing to print, which is why the gate asks for a past instead of a claim. Marriage certificate hash with civil registry attestation supplies that past: a certificate whose hash matches the registry. The nadir of the test is the date - the record predates this epoch by years, written for another purpose entirely. Faking one identity means staging that whole history, and the reef in the middle is the bill: fees, visits, and signatures collected over time. The velvet that closes it is the registry check, done in seconds.
